clue.text: Dreary versifier on way back

indicators.note: on the way back says the poet's word is read from its end to its start

parts.note: a bard is a poet, someone who writes verse

explanation.surface: A dull poet trudging home.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something drab is dull and colourless, just as dreary things are.

clue.text: Separated daughter on island, Greek one

parts.note: Crete is a Greek island, the 'one' standing for another island

explanation.surface: A daughter living apart from the family on a Greek island.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: discrete things are distinct and individually separate, not joined together.

clue.text: Kind woman in a Northern set

indicators.note: in places the northern letter within the other pieces

parts.note: to gel is to set, as a jelly does

explanation.surface: A kindly woman who belongs to a northern social circle.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a very kind, helpful woman is often called an angel.

clue.text: Unusual hassle accommodating European learner (hard case)

indicators.note: accommodating means the jumbled letters take the other two inside them
unusual means the letters of hassle are put into an uncommon order

parts.note: L is for learner, as on a learner driver's L-plate

explanation.surface: A fuss over taking in a European student.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusual' turns HASSLE into SEASHL; 'accommodating' puts EL inside it, before its final L.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: the shell of a sea creature is the hard casing it lives in.

clue.text: At Internet, men's unexpected fun?

indicators.note: unexpected suggests the letters of the three words turn up in a surprising order

parts.note: taken as written; the 's is a link meaning 'is'

explanation.surface: Men online finding unexpected amusement.
explanation.walkthrough: Only 'men' joins the fodder: the 's reads as 'is', linking wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: entertainment is amusement, things done for fun; the question mark flags the loose fit.

clue.text: Protest is over money

indicators.note: in a down clue over says the little word is turned upside down, reading upwards

parts.note: tin is old slang for money

explanation.surface: A demonstration about cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a sit-in is a protest where people occupy a place and refuse to leave.

clue.text: Competition I'd entered — that's obvious

indicators.note: entered says the shortened 'I'd' goes inside the contest word

parts.note: an event is a contest or competition
I'd written without its apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone stating plainly that they took part in a contest.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something evident is plain to see, clear and apparent.

clue.text: National emblem from barge upset?

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned over, so the boat's word reads upwards

parts.note: a keel is a flat-bottomed barge used on rivers such as the Tyne

explanation.surface: A national symbol salvaged from a capsized barge.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: this vegetable is a national emblem of Wales, worn on St David's Day.

clue.text: Some deride Green's award

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some people mock the prize given to someone called Green.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a university confers a degree as an academic award.

clue.text: Street occupied by, say, soldiers in part

indicators.note: occupied by says the street abbreviation has the other pieces inside it

parts.note: say signals an example, abbreviated eg
men is a common word for soldiers, especially the ranks

explanation.surface: Troops occupy a street, as in some part of a town.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a segment is a section or portion of a whole.

clue.text: Gourmet finally ready for this? Hardly!

definitions.text: Gourmet finally ready for this? Hardly!

indicators.note: finally takes the closing letter of the word Gourmet

parts.note: ripe means ready, as fruit ready to eat

explanation.surface: A food lover is hardly going to be prepared to eat this dish.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines: offal like this is the last thing a gourmet would welcome.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: stomach lining of cattle is a humble dish few fine diners would choose.

clue.text: Cattle stealer (no saint!) one put in charge

indicators.note: no saint says the saint abbreviation is removed from the thief's word

parts.note: a rustler steals livestock

explanation.surface: A cattle thief, far from saintly, is made the boss.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a ruler governs, the person given authority over others.

clue.text: Park worker's fury right at the start

parts.note: anger is fury, rage

explanation.surface: A park keeper's rage is justified from the outset.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'worker's' reads as 'is'; 'at the start' places R first.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a park ranger looks after a national park or countryside area.

clue.text: Cook brought round milky coffee and soft soap

indicators.note: brought round says the cooking word goes around the coffee

parts.note: to fry is to cook
a latte is coffee made with lots of steamed milk

explanation.surface: A cook serves a latte and some gentle soap.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: soft soap is persuasive praise, insincere compliments to win someone over.

clue.text: Unreliable name-plate term rewritten

indicators.note: rewritten means the letters of the phrase are set down again in a new order

explanation.surface: A word on a name-plate redone because it could not be trusted.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a temperamental machine or person behaves erratically and cannot be depended upon.

clue.text: In Low German the word for "wind"?

parts.note: mean can mean low, base or contemptible
der is the masculine form of 'the' in German

explanation.surface: A query about how the Low German language says 'wind'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low German' looks like the language, but the words split: 'Low' and 'German the'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a river or path that winds twists along a turning course.

clue.text: Tasty item in extremely exotic retreat

indicators.note: extremely takes the extreme letters, first and last, of exotic

parts.note: a lair is an animal's den or a hideaway

explanation.surface: Something delicious found in a far-flung hideaway.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: this cream-filled choux pastry is a tasty treat.

clue.text: Bringin' up dried fruit?

definitions.meaning: rearing children, with the final g dropped as the apostrophe shows

explanation.surface: A homely question about raising dried fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: The dropped g in 'Bringin'' tells you to drop the g from raising.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a dried grape is the commonest dried fruit in baking.

clue.text: Be of use — bring holy books into Bishop's place

indicators.note: into says the Bible abbreviation goes inside the bishop's word

parts.note: a see is a bishop's diocese or seat
RV is the Revised Version of the Bible

explanation.surface: Being useful by taking Bibles to the bishop's residence.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to serve is to be useful, to function for a purpose.

clue.text: With permission, starts to live in city in Thailand

indicators.note: starts to takes the opening letter of each following word

explanation.surface: Being allowed to begin living in a Thai city.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something licit is lawful, done with permission.

clue.text: Finish alongside

definitions.meaning: the end or conclusion of something

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a close is an ending, and close also means nearby, right beside.

clue.text: Chap's old record providing aid

parts.note: he refers to a man or chap
an LP is a long-playing vinyl record, an old format

explanation.surface: A man's vintage record is offered as assistance.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'Chap's' is a link meaning 'has'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: help is assistance or support given to someone.

clue.text: Church figure, cultured, learned, some recalled

indicators.note: recalled says the hidden letters are read backwards
some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A churchman described as cultivated and well read.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an elder is a senior lay official in some churches, such as the Presbyterian.

clue.text: Typical example of English mine home, hard to leave

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine

indicators.note: hard to leave says the hard abbreviation departs from the dwelling word

parts.note: taken as written
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: An English mining home that is hard to quit.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an epitome is the perfect example or embodiment of a type.

clue.text: Go through food consumed by French dad

indicators.note: consumed by says the food goes inside the French father

parts.note: pere is French for father
meat can mean food in general, as in meat and drink

explanation.surface: A French father eats his way through dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to permeate is to spread through or pervade something.

clue.text: Refuse requests of Democrat initially entering New York

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of each of the two words before New York

explanation.surface: Turning down a Democrat's pleas on arrival in New York.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to deny someone is to turn down what they ask for.
